newsitem.title: USA: Calif. budget may not include welfare plan - Gov..
newsitem.headline: Calif. budget may not include welfare plan - Gov..

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson and the state Senate's president said on Tuesday lawmakers may be forced to adopt the 1997-1998 state budget without welfare reform.
"Obviously it is possible to get closure on the budget without welfare," Wilson, a Republican, said. Senate President Bill Lockyer, a Democrat, said he agreed.
They made their comments at separate news conferences in Sacramento one day after Wilson vetoed the welfare reform plan drafted by state Democrats.

Republicans contend that the Democratic plan would be too generous and far too expensive. Wilson's office said the Democratic package would cost the state $1 billion more each year than the governor's own welfare proposal.

Welfare reform has been a major stumbling block for lawmakers negotiating California's budget for the 1997-1998 fiscal year, which began July 1. The state's Constitutional budget deadline was June 15.
